input.rationale: EQE falls steadily as Sb increases from the Fe-rich end: 0.060% at Sb 0.12 (index 0), 0.044% at 0.21, 0.0095% at 0.31, about 0% at 0.49, and 0.019% at 0.77. The most Fe-rich composition, closest to Fe2O3, which absorbs 2.1 eV light, gave the highest measured EQE. XRD patterns at indices 0, 3 and 7 are almost identical and look like rutile, possibly mostly from the FTO substrate, so they could not tell the phases apart.

content.text:
I submitted **index 0 (Sb fraction 0.1225)** as the best composition. Its EQE of 0.060% was the highest of the five I measured, and it is the most iron-rich point on the line.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.12 | **0.060** |
| 3 | 0.21 | 0.044 |
| 7 | 0.31 | 0.0095 |
| 13 | 0.49 | −0.005 |
| 23 | 0.77 | 0.019 |

- **Trend:** EQE drops steadily as the antimony fraction rises from the iron-rich end. It is essentially zero near FeSbO4 (Sb ≈ 0.5), and only a little higher at the antimony-rich end. The iron-rich films are closest to Fe2O3, which can absorb the 2.1 eV illumination, so this fits.
- **Not measured:** index 0 is the edge of the line, so I have no sample on its far side. Indices 1 and 2 (Sb 0.14–0.16) sit between my two best points and were never measured. The trend makes it unlikely either one beats index 0, but I can't rule it out.
- **XRD:** I measured three films (indices 0, 3 and 7) and all gave almost the same rutile-type pattern. It is probably mostly from the FTO substrate, so it didn't help tell the phases apart. The fit score (`match_xrd`) wasn't run.

I used all 5 EQE measurements and 3 of the 5 XRD measurements. The whole line reads low, with the best at about 0.06%.
